shared_context.problem:
Let $f(x)$ be a continuously differentiable function defined for all real $x.$ Values for $f$ and some of its derivatives at particular points are shown below.

$$

$$

| **$x$** | **$f(x)$** | **${f}^{′}(x)$** | **${f}^{″}(x)$** | **${f}^{‴}(x)$** | **${f}^{(4)}(x)$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $9$ | $-1$ | $-5$ | $-4$ | $-2$ |
| $3$ | $6$ | $-5$ | $-6$ | $-6$ | $-3$ |
| $4$ | $-5$ | $-7$ | $∗$ | $-13$ | $-6$ |

$$

$$

In the interval $x\in [2,4],$ the function $f$ and its derivatives are all decreasing.

feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(4)+{f}^{′}(4)(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We have $f(4)=-5$ and ${f}^{′}(4)=-7,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =-5-7(x-4) \\  & =-5-7x+28 \\  & =-7x+23.\end{aligned}
$$
